trajectory_summary: This is a clean, low-friction booking call: the customer arrives curious rather than resistant, answers verify questions fluidly, retrieves his bill unprompted, and self-initiates spouse inclusion at scheduling. The rep runs the structure competently and lands a dated, timed appointment with texted confirmation, though several personalization and flip opportunities (state-incentive interest, high-usage bill, adult co-owners) were captured but not leveraged into stronger curiosity or handoff value.
outcome_dispute: The call should be tagged booked, not left ambiguous — a specific day (Wednesday the 5th) and time (2:30 PM) were confirmed and a text-confirmation number was captured.

observed_outcome.quote: 02:30, please. Okay. Sounds good. So I'll go ahead and get that on our calendar. That's Wednesday, the fifth, at 02:30PM.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time were agreed and confirmed, and the wife (co-owner via the spousal decision protocol) was proactively brought onto the call and confirmed available for that slot.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: On the average, I'd say it's somewhere around $400.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the bill (and later the kWh detail) but only responded with acknowledgment ('Yeah. Dang. Yeah. That is quite the range there. That's pretty crazy.') and never turned it into a reason to act; the flip should have landed around 03:07-03:16 or again at 06:24 when the customer emphasized high consumption.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: No. I've been interested for a long time. Prices are coming down, and some of the offsets being offered by the state are attractive.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the interest question and got a specific, usable answer (price trend + state incentives), but only paraphrased it once generically ('just kinda looking into it now for the the programs and just the extra benefits') and never referenced it again at booking or in the button-up.

script_coverage.quote: Hey. This is Joel with ION. I just got a request that you were looking into solar for your home.
I'm just curious. What got you interested in solar?
I have your address here as the 49 Starview Place in Lancaster, Virginia. Is that correct?
Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you at all?
the roof up there, is it just the classic asphalt shingles?
for utilities, are you guys going through Dominion there?
how much would you say just an average, electric bills cost, costing you guys?
would just need to have a form of taxable income and a credit score of six fifty or higher
have you seen a solar design for the home before?
do you usually get those Northern Neck bills online or through the mail?
would a morning or afternoon time work best for you guys?
I'll send you a text, just with that day and time, you know, just so it doesn't creep up on you guys.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: flipping the bill/usage pain into leverage
primary_coaching_focus.quote: We we consume a lot of electricity.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep captured a strong bill anchor ($300-620/mo, high dual-panel usage) but never converted it into an emotional flip against the utility or reinforced it at booking; this is the single highest-leverage miss on an otherwise clean call.

key_moments.quote: Yes. Our son our daughter and son.
key_moments.stewart_read: Frederick discloses adult children on the title, but the rep says only 'Okay. Awesome' and moves to the next verify item without asking whether the son or daughter should be included in the appointment or credit-qualified separately.

key_moments.quote: No. I've been interested for a long time. Prices are coming down, and some of the offsets being offered by the state are attractive.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a specific, personalizable interest reason (price trend + state incentives) that could anchor both the pitch and the text follow-up tieback, but the rep only reflects it back generically ('just kinda looking into it now for the the programs and just the extra benefits') and never returns to it.

key_moments.quote: Well, it's classic asphalt shingles, but it's not a classic roof.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers detail about roof shape suggesting easy install, and the rep responds warmly and accurately ('you're getting, you know, more sun throughout the day, not having to worry about the steep pitches'), which is a good micro-affirmation of a positive install signal.

key_moments.quote: Probably around 3,000 k w a year.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer self-reports high dual-200-amp-panel usage and a bill ranging $300-$620, but the rep's only response is a flat math confirmation ('I'll just do the math there. So 3,000 times 12 will tell us kind of your annual usage') with no emotional reflection of the pain represented by that range.
